rubric.reason: Task 10's **MIRROR** line reads literally 'TBD - needs validation' (plan line 513: "- **MIRROR**: `TBD - needs validation` — no existing relay runbook/checklist artifact was found by this plan's grounding pass to anchor a structural precedent..."). R3 scans every task's MIRROR/VALIDATE lines for TBD and permits it only in ## Notes and the ## Risks and Mitigations mitigation column — Task 10's MIRROR line is not on that permitted list, so this is a hard structural fail regardless of the narrative justification given inline (that no existing pattern was found to mirror).

None of Tasks 1-10 (### Task 1: CREATE plugins/relay/commands/relay-visual-review.md; ### Task 2: UPDATE plugins/relay/agents/docs-updater.md; ### Task 3: UPDATE scripts/generate-final-report.mjs; ### Task 4: UPDATE plugins/relay/commands/relay-qa-report.md; ### Task 5: UPDATE plugins/relay/commands/relay-execute.md; ### Task 6: UPDATE plugins/relay/commands/relay-pr.md; ### Task 7: UPDATE docs/api-reference.md; ### Task 8: UPDATE docs/context/architecture.md; ### Task 9: UPDATE documentation/ site (three-file registration rule); ### Task 10: CREATE docs/design/dogfood-runbook.md) contains a literal AC-A<i> or AC-<N> token reference anywhere in its ACTION/MIRROR/VALIDATE body text, and none carry an explicit 'infrastructure / scaffolding' annotation that would exempt them. Each task is semantically traceable to an Acceptance Criteria item, but the deterministic grep this check specifies finds zero literal token citations plan-wide.

Declared test_frameworks: ["node:test"]; plan_phase_type: feature (no scaffold/docs/foundation exemption branch applies). No VALIDATE command invokes a mismatched framework (e.g. pytest/jest/go test): 9 of 10 tasks' VALIDATE blocks are set -euo pipefail-guarded OS/filesystem + grep content-existence checks appropriate for markdown/config-only edits, and Task 3 (the sole .mjs-touching task) invokes `node --check` (same executable family as the declared node:test runner). Behavioral node:test coverage for scripts/generate-final-report.mjs is authored downstream by the test-writer/test-reviewer pair after the Implementer + Code Review, per this repo's documented test-after convention (## Notes; Risks row 1; docs/context/methodology.md) — VALIDATE commands baked into the plan's own Step-by-Step Tasks were never expected to invoke the framework directly for prompt/markdown-editing tasks.

## Mandatory Reading's row for `plugins/relay/commands/relay-pr.md` (lines 300–330) says: "confirms `/relay-pr` already calls `generate-final-report.mjs` unconditionally, so extending the script is sufficient wiring; no new script invocation is needed in this file." ## Summary repeats the same claim: "already invoked unconditionally by `/relay-pr` Phase 3 Step 3". But `relay-pr.md:300-330` itself reads: "Check whether both `PRPs/reports/<feature>/run.json` and `PRPs/reports/<feature>/test-review.json` exist. **Full body path (both artifacts exist):** Run: node .../generate-final-report.mjs ..." immediately followed by a **Minimal body path (no test artifacts or run.json absent)** branch that never calls the script at all ("Do not write `PRPs/reports/<feature>/final-report.md` on the minimal-body path."). The invocation is conditional on both artifacts existing, not unconditional — Task 6's own ACTION text is more careful ("already invoked unconditionally on the full-body path"), but the Summary and the Mandatory Reading Why column both drop that qualifier, which could mislead a reader into believing the new Visual Fidelity section always reaches the PR body when it is in fact silently absent whenever run.json/test-review.json don't exist yet.

Declared test_frameworks: ["node:test"]; plan_phase_type: feature (no scaffold/docs/foundation exemption branch applies). No VALIDATE command in ## Step-by-Step Tasks invokes any test-framework binary at all (matched or mismatched) — 9 of 10 tasks' VALIDATE blocks are set -euo pipefail-guarded OS/filesystem + grep content-existence assertions appropriate for markdown/config-only edits, and Task 3 (the sole .mjs-touching task) invokes `node --check` for a syntax check. This check's name targets MISMATCH (asserting the wrong framework), which requires a command to claim a framework identity in the first place; none do. Behavioral node:test coverage for scripts/generate-final-report.mjs is authored downstream by the test-writer/test-reviewer pair after the Implementer + Code Review per this repo's declared test-after routing (## Notes; Risks row 1; docs/context/methodology.md tdd: false) — the plan's own per-task VALIDATE gates run before that suite exists, so they cannot invoke it.
